pipeline_result.response: Nuptse is closer to the tallest mountain in the Solar System than Gasherbrum II, which is located 40 kilometers away from Nuptse.
retrieved_context: Nuptse: Nuptse or Nubtse (Sherpa: ནུབ་རྩེ། नुबचे, Wylie: Nub rtse) is a mountain in the Khumbu region of the Mahalangur Himal, in the Nepalese Himalayas.  It lies two kilometres WSW of Mount Everest.  Nubtse is Tibetan for "west peak", as it is the western segment of the Lhotse-Nubtse massif.

List of tallest mountains in the Solar System: This is a list of the tallest mountains in the Solar System.  The tallest peak or peaks on worlds where significant mountains have been measured are given; in some cases, the tallest peaks of different classes on a world are also listed.  At 21.9 km, the enormous shield volcano Olympus Mons on Mars is the tallest mountain on any planet.  For 40 years, following its discovery in 1971, it was the tallest mountain known in the Solar System.  However, in 2011, the central peak of the crater Rheasilvia on the asteroid and protoplanet Vesta was found to be of comparable height.

Tongshanjiabu: Tongshanjiabu () is a mountain in the Himalayas.  At 7,207 m tall, Tongshanjiabu is the 103rd tallest mountain in the world.  It sits in the disputed border territory between Bhutan and China.  Tongshanjiabu has never been officially climbed.
